cases.source: info-response block: body is any-char text, closed by %info off before the response

class_descriptions.domain: Domain objects, one per registered domain

cases.source: class-line in each of its three alternates (description, version time-stamp, meta-field/meta-value), two records each closed by a bare %class
directive-record with the description alternate and an attribute-name/value alternate, closed by a bare %directive
display-record: RFC 2167 leaves the display shape to the server, so this pins the name/attribute grouping that a bare %display closes
schema-record per attribute: each attribute of a class is its own record, closed by a bare %schema, which is why the terminator rather than the class names the group
soa-line in every alternate: authority, the four digit timers, the serial time-stamp, three e-mails, a host-port primary, and one extension field
status-line in all seven alternates; on-off is lower case as Appendix B spells it, which is not how the RFC's own section 3.3 example prints it
xfer-record: transfer object lines, each record ended by a bare %xfer, so the groups are told apart by their terminator rather than by a blank line
a blank line separates records, so a domain record and a network record may share one response; a class change inside a record is still rejected
referral-record of two consecutive referral lines, one with a numeric host-port and one with a host-name, then a partial object record
query-string with the trailing wildcard both readings agree on; each client line is also round-tripped through registrata.query while the case is built

DERIVED FROM SECTION 3.4, NOT Appendix B: 3.4 allows a leading '*' (its prose says the wildcard may appear in the front and/or at the end) while Appendix B puts the '*' only at the end. The bytes are derivable under Appendix B only as a literal query-char star, which is a different search; registrata implements 3.4

quoted-query-char exercised with the space and tab it adds to query-char; an inner double quote is in the production too, but registrata.query rejects one anywhere in a value, so that alternative is a documented deviation instead of a case
attribute-query and bin-boolean; query is left-recursive as written, so a chain is read as nesting with a depth limit, exactly as the grammar inventory notes

every single-line client directive in one session; directive lines are client-to-server bytes, so they are unmatched lines to the response parser and what is pinned is that the transcript is still readable

xfer-dir in its four shapes. attribute-def is optional in every part, so *attribute-def can loop on the empty string - the bare form below is legal and is why a parser cannot rely on it to make progress
notify-dir in each of its five alternates: badref and recurref carry a referral-query (a referral-url plus the query that caused it), update/inssec/delsec carry a host-port and an authority area
security-dir: the directive line, its security-payload, and the optional -security off. Appendix B spells the method and data as an open set, so an extension method is as valid as password or pgp
register-dir in the add form: register-on with the literal add, the maintainer-id, the register-add payload of register-line data, register-off, and the object-id reply
register-dir in the mod form: register-mod is one or more register-lines, the literal _NEW_, then the replacement payload; the reply carries the Updated time-stamp
register-dir in the del form; register-del is only the payload, so the third alternate of register-off-response (a plain response) is the one that applies
x-dir and x-response: the X namespace is defined only as "the server may say anything", so an x-response is any run of lines terminated by a response

one server dialogue carrying every recognised response family. responses and server-returns are protocol-wide alternations, and x-response alone accepts any text ending in a response, so the witness is the whole span rather than one line

description: RFC 2167 RWhois transcript corpus. Valid cases assert parsed structure and, where marked, parser round-trips. Malformed cases pin the failure contract: only registrata.errors.RwhoisError subclasses may escape. Every entry lists the ABNF productions its transcript exercises under "abnf".
